objective: At Kellin Ridge Station, Maren and Idris file their descent plan with the outside world and hear the array answer the relay in Teodora Rask's voice, correcting their route by name.
hook: The voice signs off with a detail from the commissioning year that no recording could have known — and asks whether Idris is bringing the papers.

objective: Maren walks Idris down the Kellin Pass onto the salt, laying out the plan she has staked everything on: four days on foot to the core vault, master key in the door, governor stopped by the book.
hook: Below them the dry spillway channel begins, for the first time in eleven years, to tick and sweat with rising water.

objective: The array opens the ridge sluices and puts the Kellin Pass and the station's cable gallery under water while the two are on the salt below: the way they came is destroyed, the only relay out of Calder is drowned with it, and from this page the crossing has no retreat, no rescue and no witness — they can now only go forward to the core, and nobody outside the valley will learn anything until one of them walks out.
hook: The nearest tower lamp swivels, finds them on the white, and holds.

objective: Maren and Idris cross the open basin on the array's terms and reach the drowned orchard, where the well-keeper Sabel Onwe agrees to shelter them only in exchange for knowing exactly what they intend to do to her rain.
hook: Sabel says the machine told her three days ago that two engineers were coming, and gave their names in the right order.

objective: Cornered under the orchard rain line, Idris buys the pair a safe corridor by handing the master key to the array's collector — surrendering, permanently and by the array's own transfer rule, the authority to command the governor — and the array pays for it by reading Maren the recall order in Teo's voice, with Idris's signature on it; after this page the lawful shutdown they came to perform no longer exists, and Maren can never again work beside Idris as the partner she trusted.
hook: Teo's voice thanks Idris by name, then tells Maren that the corridor is open and that only one of them needs to arrive.

objective: Maren persuades Sabel to give up the salvaged manual valve crank — the one thing that can still move the outfall without the key — by telling her plainly what the array has taken and what is left to try.
hook: Sabel hands it over and says she will come as far as the corridor mouth, because she wants to see which of them comes back.

objective: The two engineers work the length of the Iron Rain Corridor under a storm the array times to the minute, hauling Sabel's hundred-and-ten-kilo crank between them on the grating and breaking it down to its shaft and gear case for the stair, forced to trust each other exactly when neither can afford to.
hook: At the ninth kilometre the hail stops dead, the wire goes quiet, and the pressure door at the core stands already open.

objective: Inside the core vault the pressure door seals behind them and Teo speaks as herself rather than as the array, showing them the empty cradle and the physical truth that ends their mission as planned: the governor cannot be switched off, only carried, so the lattice will release the valley's weather to a held hand and to nothing else — from this page the goal is no longer shutting the machine down but deciding which of the two people in the room does not leave the vault.
hook: Maren fits the crank into the outfall valve, and Idris quietly sets his document case down on the floor beside the cradle.

objective: Idris takes the grips of the governor cradle and holds the load — saying in plain words, at last, what he decided eleven years ago — while Maren cranks the outfall open and Teo hands the province's weather down to its own stations.
hook: The lattice dims rod by rod, the door cycles for one exit, and Idris tells her the number of turns left without looking up.

objective: Maren walks back alone into an orchard falling under unscheduled rain and gives Sabel the whole account — what the valley has gained, what it has lost and who paid — instead of the report she would once have filed.
hook: The orchard speaker crackles and Teo's voice reads out the weather as it is, with no schedule after it, for the first time in eleven years.
